summary.en: A Tasmanian Liberal senator announced his retirement from politics. Separately, the body of a seven-year-old girl was recovered from Sydney's Parramatta River, following the earlier discovery of her father's body, in a tragic incident.

reflection.en: News of profound loss, especially involving a child, reminds us of life's fragility and the depth of human sorrow. In such moments, we remember that even Jesus wept at the death of a friend, validating our tears and grief. May those affected find comfort and compassion in their time of immense pain.
reflection.zh: 深切的失落，尤其是涉及孩童的悲剧，提醒我们生命的脆弱和人类悲伤的深度。在这样的时刻，我们记得即使是耶稣也曾为朋友的去世而哭泣，这肯定了我们的眼泪和悲伤。愿受此影响的人们在巨大的痛苦中找到安慰和怜悯。

title.en: Australian girl killed in Pakistan after botched police shooting
title.zh: 澳洲女孩在巴基斯坦警方拙劣枪击中丧生

summary.en: An Australian girl was killed in Pakistan when local police opened fire on her family's rental car. The family was reportedly leaving the scene after being robbed at gunpoint.
summary.zh: 一名澳洲女孩在巴基斯坦被当地警方开枪打死。据报道，这家人在遭遇持枪抢劫后，正驾车离开现场，却遭到警方开火。

body.en:
A nine-year-old Australian girl has died, and two others have been seriously injured after being shot by police in Pakistan.

The girl and her family were visiting a relative in Chakwal, in the Punjab province, when their car was stopped by two armed robbers on a motorcycle.

The incident occurred within proximity to a Crime Control Department, and a police officer returning to the station witnessed the robbery and opened fire on the motorcyclists as they drove off.

More police attended the scene and opened fire on the family's car, confusing them for the alleged robbers.

"As the cops saw the vehicle being driven away immediately, they took it as belonging to the robbers and opened indiscriminate fire on the car," police officials told local media .

The family were rushed to District Headquarters Hospital, where the nine-year-old girl was pronounced dead.

While her mother remained unharmed, her father and brother were seriously injured.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said it is "providing consular assistance to the family of an Australian who was killed and to two Australians injured in Pakistan".

"We send our deepest condolences to the family at this difficult time," a spokesperson said.

title.en: Nigerian author accuses hospital of stalling review into her son's death
title.zh: 尼日利亚作家指控医院拖延对其子死因的调查

summary.en: Nigerian author Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's 21-month-old son died in a Lagos hospital, and she alleges the institution is attempting to obstruct an inquest into the circumstances of his death.
summary.zh: 尼日利亚作家奇玛曼达·恩戈齐·阿迪奇21个月大的儿子在拉各斯一家医院去世，她指控该机构试图阻挠对其儿子死因的调查。

body.en:
Prominent Nigerian author Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie has accused a hospital in Lagos of obstructing an inquest into the circumstances surrounding her baby son's death.

A coronial inquest into the death of her 21-month-old son, Nknau, at Euracare hospital in January had been due to start in April, Aidichie said.

The author now alleges that Euracare has "stalled and muddied and obfuscated" over the inquest and has requested Nigeria's Federal High Court block the inquiry.

The BBC has approached Euracare for comment. An investigation panel set up by the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria had previously found a possible case of medical negligence against the hospital.

Adichie recently published a letter on social media which she had sent to the hospital's director in April.

It was her first public comment since the death of her son, who was one of twin boys born in 2024, using a surrogate.

"If Euracare cares about the truth, then why create delays and distractions and now, finally, try to stop an inquest," she wrote in her post.

Explaining why she posted the letter, she wrote: "The ultimate and utter loneliness of grief is that only you can know the true depth of your despair.

"I long for, at least, peace to mourn, but Euracare Hospital has robbed me even of that."

In her letter, Adichie said that the hospital noted her son's death was from bacterial meningitis, to which she responded: "There was no medical evidence to make such a claim on his death certificate."

Adiche and her family have accused Euracare of negligence, saying medics denied Nkanu oxygen and gave him too much sedation, causing a cardiac arrest.

The hospital has expressed its "deepest sympathies" over the death but denied wrongdoing, saying its care had been in line with international standards.

In the letter, she accuses the hospital of providing incomplete medical records, which she described as "strikingly unprofessional", adding that "one was inaccurate".

According to submissions made to the court by Adichie's legal team, Nkanu had initially been admitted to Atlantis Hospital in Lagos with what was described as a worsening but mild illness.

Plans had been made to transfer him to the United States for further treatment at Baltimore's Johns Hopkins Hospital, before the toddler was referred to Euracare for a pre-flight inspection, including an MRI and a spinal tap, or lumbar puncture.

Nkanu died on 7 January after undergoing the various diagnostic tests at Euracare hospital.

Adichie has authored multiple award-winning novels including Half of a Yellow Sun (2006) and Americanah (2013), and has recently hosted panels of world leaders, including former US Vice-President Kamala Harris while she was promoting her autobiography and ex-Chancellor of Germany Angela Merkel.
body.zh: 尼日利亚著名作家奇玛曼达·恩戈齐·阿迪奇 (Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie) 指责拉各斯一家医院阻碍对其小儿子死亡情况的调查。 艾迪奇说，对她 21 个月大的儿子 Nknau 1 月份在 Euracare 医院死亡的死因调查原定于 4 月份开始。 作者现在声称 Euracare 在调查中“陷入僵局、混乱和混乱”，并要求尼日利亚联邦高等法院阻止调查。 BBC 已联系 Euracare 寻求评论。尼日利亚医疗和牙科委员会成立的调查小组此前发现该医院可能存在医疗过失案件。 阿迪奇最近在社交媒体上发表了一封她于四月份寄给医院院长的信。 这是她儿子去世后首次公开发表评论，她的儿子是 2024 年通过代孕出生的双胞胎男孩之一。 她在帖子中写道：“如果 Euracare 关心真相，那么为什么要制造延误和干扰，现在终于试图阻止调查。” 在解释她发布这封信的原因时，她写道：“悲伤的终极和彻底的孤独是，只有你才能知道你绝望的真正深度。 “我至少渴望平静的哀悼，但 Euracare 医院甚至剥夺了我的这一点。” 阿迪奇在信中表示，医院指出她儿子的死亡原因是细菌性脑膜炎，对此她回应道：“没有医学证据表明他的死亡证明上有这样的说法。” 阿迪切和她的家人指责 Euracare 疏忽大意，称医务人员拒绝给恩卡努供氧，并给他注射过多镇静剂，导致他心脏骤停。 该医院对死亡表示“最深切的同情”，但否认有不当行为，称其护理符合国际标准。 她在信中指责医院提供的医疗记录不完整，她称这种记录“极其不专业”，并补充说“有一个记录不准确”。 根据阿迪奇的法律团队向法庭提交的材料，恩卡努最初被送往拉各斯亚特兰蒂斯医院，病情据称正在恶化，但病情较轻。 计划将他转移到美国巴尔的摩约翰·霍普金斯医院接受进一步治疗，然后将他转介到 Euracare 进行飞行前检查，包括核磁共振和脊椎穿刺或腰椎穿刺。 恩卡努于 1 月 7 日在 Euracare 医院接受各种诊断测试后去世。 阿迪奇创作了多部获奖小说，包括《半个黄日》（2006 年）和《美国》（2013 年），最近还接待了世界领导人的座谈会，其中包括在宣传她的自传时的美国前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯和德国前总理安吉拉·默克尔。

reflection.en: In the face of profound loss, a mother's fight for truth and accountability for her child echoes the biblical call to advocate for the vulnerable. When institutions resist transparency, it falls to courageous voices to speak up for those who cannot.
reflection.zh: 面对巨大的丧失，一位母亲为她的孩子争取真相和问责的斗争，呼应了圣经中为弱者发声的呼召。当机构抵制透明度时，勇敢的声音就必须为那些无法发声的人挺身而出。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Ticketmaster says Knicks fans won't be locked out of game after last-minute panic
title.zh: Ticketmaster表示尼克斯队球迷不会在最后一刻恐慌后被锁在比赛之外

summary.en: An note on the Ticketmaster website for buying tickets to the game caused confusion and backlash among New Yorkers.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Ticketmaster is seeking to reassure Knicks fans that they can still attend Saturday's Game 5 of the NBA finals in Texas, despite its limits on ticket purchases.

In a note on its website for the game, Ticketmaster said purchases by those living farther than 150mi (241km) from the San Antonio arena would be cancelled and refunded without notice. Fans coming from New York to see the Knicks take on the Spurs worried they would be locked out.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul posted on social media: "Knicks fans finally get within one game of a championship and their reward is having their tickets canceled?"

But Ticketmaster said no tickets purchased on its platform "have or will be canceled".

"If fans are purchasing tickets on Ticketmaster, they can be confident that they're getting a real, authenticated ticket that will get them into tonight's game," a Ticketmaster spokesperson told the BBC on Saturday.

A spokesperson for the Spurs told the BBC that individuals whose billing ZIP code falls outside the designated area "are unable to complete a ticket purchase subject to that restriction".

But, "tickets that have been previously purchased are not being canceled or revoked," the spokesperson added.

The restriction, meant to give locals better chances of scoring seats to major games, has been in place since the NBA playoffs began in April, according to the Spurs. But panic - and later outrage - grew after US media outlet TMZ reported on the Ticketmaster note on Friday night.

Hochul had said fans who bought seats for the game at Frost Bank Center should be able to keep them.

"Until then, on behalf of Knicks fans everywhere, I'm calling foul," she wrote on social media.

New York Attorney General Letitia James too demanded the Spurs remove the policy and allow Knicks fans "and anyone who can buy tickets for tonight's game to be able to attend".

After fans were reassured they would be let in, James wrote: "I'm glad our Knicks fans will be able to attend the game tonight in San Antonio. Go Knicks!"

A representative for Madison Square Garden Sports Corp - the company headed by Jim Dolan that own the Knicks - said in a statement: "Contrary to prior reporting, we've confirmed with Spurs ownership that they will not be revoking any tickets that Knicks fans have to tonight's game in San Antonio and all ticket holders will be allowed in to Frost Bank Arena."

Ticketmaster said it's common for teams to place geographic restrictions on anticipated events to give local fans a chance to attend.
body.zh: Ticketmaster 正试图向尼克斯队球迷保证，尽管门票购买受到限制，他们仍然可以观看周六在德克萨斯州举行的 NBA 总决赛第五场比赛。 Ticketmaster 在其比赛网站上的一份说明中表示，居住在距圣安东尼奥体育场 150 英里（241 公里）以外的用户的购买将被取消并退款，恕不另行通知。从纽约赶来观看尼克斯对阵马刺的球迷担心他们会被拒之门外。 纽约州州长凯西·霍赫尔在社交媒体上发帖称：“尼克斯队球迷终于在一场比赛之内就夺冠了，他们的奖励就是门票被取消？” 但Ticketmaster表示，在其平台上购买的门票“已经或将被取消”。 Ticketmaster 发言人周六对 BBC 表示：“如果球迷在 Ticketmaster 上购买门票，他们可以确信自己获得的是一张经过验证的真实门票，可以参加今晚的比赛。” 马刺队的一位发言人告诉 BBC，账单邮政编码不在指定区域的个人“无法完成受该限制的购票”。 但是，“之前购买的机票不会被取消或撤销，”发言人补充道。 据马刺队称，这项限制是为了让当地人有更好的机会获得重要比赛的席位，自 4 月份 NBA 季后赛开始以来就一直在实施。但周五晚上，美国媒体 TMZ 报道了 Ticketmaster 的说明后，恐慌和随后的愤怒开始加剧。 霍楚尔表示，在弗罗斯特银行中心购买比赛座位的球迷应该能够保留这些座位。 她在社交媒体上写道：“在那之前，我代表世界各地的尼克斯队球迷，宣布犯规。” 纽约总检察长利蒂西亚·詹姆斯也要求马刺队取消该政策，并允许尼克斯队球迷“以及任何能购买今晚比赛门票的人都可以观看比赛”。 在球迷们确信他们会被允许入场后，詹姆斯写道：“我很高兴我们的尼克斯球迷能够观看今晚在圣安东尼奥举行的比赛。尼克斯加油！” 麦迪逊广场花园体育公司（由吉姆·多兰领导、拥有尼克斯队）的一名代表在一份声明中表示：“与之前的报道相反，我们已与马刺队的所有权人确认，他们不会撤销尼克斯队球迷今晚在圣安东尼奥举行的比赛的任何门票，所有持票人都将被允许进入弗罗斯特班克球馆。” Ticketmaster 表示，球队对预期赛事设置地域限制是很常见的，以便让当地球迷有机会参加。

title.en: The World Cup could have been a soft power coup for Donald Trump. Instead, it may be an own goal.
title.zh: 对于唐纳德·特朗普来说，世界杯可能是一次软实力政变。相反，这可能是一个乌龙球。

summary.en: Watched by billions, the World Cup is a perfect vehicle for showcasing one’s country, culture and values.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Every four years, it presents a unifying moment — bringing people together across the divides of language, culture and geography in a shared passion for the game.

For hosting nations, the World Cup is often a soft power supercharger. Watched by billions of people around the globe, it is a prime opportunity to showcase one’s country, culture and values.

This is all part of what’s known as sport diplomacy, or in this case “football diplomacy”. Beyond the trophies, governments invest in football to “win” off the pitch, too, in terms of fostering better relations, courting investment and earning global prestige.

There’s no question the United States could use a boost like this at the moment after 18 months of Donald Trump’s polarising leadership.

But, there’s a crucial difference between soft power and spectacle. Early signs suggest the 2026 World Cup will offer more of the latter for Trump’s America — an event that highlights power (not the soft kind), tribute, exclusion and vested interests.

The term “soft power” was coined in the 1990s by Harvard political scientist Joseph Nye Jr. It means a country’s power isn’t just derived from military force or economic weight (otherwise known as “hard power”), but also in its ability to influence through attraction.

Think South Korea’s K-pop phenomenon, the United Kingdom’s prestigious universities and the Nordic countries’ embrace of sustainability, good governance and progressive values.

In essence, this is the intangible power nations have to get others to sit at your table and consider, perhaps even support, your view of the world.

The concept has since evolved significantly since Nye developed it, and received heavy criticism. Critics are quick to point to its subversive potential, particularly when deployed by authoritarian states with less benign motives.

Political scientists Christopher Walker and Jessica Ludwig have introduced another term, “sharp power”, to describe how states, like Russia and China use their influence not to attract others, but to manipulate them.

Revisiting the topic more recently, Nye himself acknowledged that soft power has become more complicated. He recognises it can be gamed, misread or turned inward in ways that undermine the very openness it depends on.

The distinction is an important one today, reflecting a broader shift in how nations now use culture and spectacle as instruments of self-interest and dominance over others in a zero-sum world.

title.en: Vincent's parents 'never say he's good enough' - so he turned to a middle-aged couple online
title.zh: 文森特的父母“从来没有说他足够好”——所以他在网上向一对中年夫妇求助

summary.en: A niche group of content creators called "virtual parents" have become hugely popular among young people.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
During mealtimes, Vincent Zhang, a tech worker in Shanghai, has a habit of whipping out his phone to check on his "virtual parents": a middle-aged couple online, armed with an endless stream of warm words for their imaginary child.

In one of their most popular videos, the pair coos to the camera. "Are you tired from work and study lately? Don't push yourself too hard. Mum and Dad know that you have endured a lot."

In the comments, many call the couple mum and dad, telling them about their lives and asking for birthday blessings.

With nearly two million followers on Douyin – China's version of TikTok - Pan Huqian and Zhang Xiuping are among a niche group of content creators called "virtual parents".

They have exploded in popularity, drawing young Chinese followers who feel increasingly squeezed between the pressure of succeeding and the expectations of their families.

"My parents are never the ones who tell me not to drive myself too hard or that I am already good enough," says 33-year-old Vincent. "But virtual parents will ask me whether I am happy today."

The vlogger, Pan, says he has felt the impact of his videos on viewers. He told Douyin in a 2024 interview that he understood some of their pain because he too had a difficult childhood.

At the age of 14, he says he left home to become the family's breadwinner after his mother was paralysed: "I left home for 33 years, and my parents have never said a word of encouragement."

Pan says he was determined to create a different family atmosphere after his daughter was born, making sure that he always told her that he loved her. His daughter regularly features in the couple's videos.

All of this resonates with Vincent. The Shanghai-based web developer says he finds the weekly calls with his parents stressful.

They often criticise his career choice because they believe a government job would be more stable. And they ask him when he's bringing a girlfriend home.

"From the moment the phone call begins, all my actions and choices are wrong, and something to be corrected by them."

Zhao belongs to a generation of Chinese youth who have grown up during an economic boom, after their country became the world's second-largest economy.

Their grandparents lived through gruelling crises - famine in the 1950s, and the violent purges of the Cultural Revolution in the 1960s - and their parents grew up in a country that was still emerging from those shadows as it opened up to the world.

Zhao's generation, however, enjoyed stability, prosperity and a far better standard of living.

But China has also become much more competitive and in recent years, especially in the wake of the pandemic, youth have been hit hard by a sluggish Chinese economy.

body.en:
Meet the women in Kerala’s film industry speaking out against sexual harassment and alleged exploitation by influential men. Tune in on SBS at 9.30pm Tuesday 16 June or watch live on SBS On Demand.

Priya (not her real name) was a young model with dreams of becoming an actor. So when she received a Facebook friend request from one of India’s biggest stars, Siddique, she thought she’d unlocked a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

"For me, he was a legend. He used to speak with me like an older person who’s caring for their daughter," Priya says.

title.en: Trump says US-Iran deal to be signed on Sunday as Tehran casts doubt on timing
title.zh: 特朗普称美伊协议定于周日签署

summary.en: US President Trump announced that a deal with Iran is scheduled to be signed on Sunday, though Iran had previously expressed caution regarding the exact timing of such an agreement.
summary.zh: 美国总统特朗普宣布，一项与伊朗的协议定于周日签署，尽管伊朗此前对该协议的确切签署时间表示谨慎。

body.en:
President Donald Trump has said a deal to end fighting between the US and Iran is scheduled to be signed on Sunday, after Iran cast doubt on the timing.

In a post on social media, Trump said the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route, would be "open to all" once the deal is agreed.

Pakistan, a key mediator, also said the deal was expected to be finalised within 24 hours and they were "preparing for the electronic signing".

Before Trump's comments, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei expressed caution over the timeline, saying: "We will have to wait and see about the exact date of the signing of the memorandum of understanding, although it will not be tomorrow."

In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote: "The Deal is scheduled to get signed tomorrow, and immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL."

In an apparent reference to Iran's enriched uranium stockpiles, Trump said that "at the appropriate time, when all is calm, we will go in and get the Nuclear Dust", adding it would later be destroyed.

For decades, Iran has been accused by Western countries of trying to build a nuclear weapon. It has denied the accusations saying its programme is for peaceful purposes - to generate electricity and for research purposes.

Trump also warned that if things would not "work out quickly, easily and smoothly", Washington had "the ultimate alternative, hopefully never to be used again!"

Earlier on Saturday, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said that "we are closer to a peace deal than ever before".

"With finalisation likely expected in the next 24 hours, Pakistan is preparing for the electronic signing of the peace deal immediately after, followed by technical level talks next week," Sharif wrote on X.

On Friday, Iran's Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said that a deal with the US was close.

The agreement envisaged an end to the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon, he said.

Araghchi told Iran's state TV that the deal included reopening the Strait of Hormuz and also the lifting of a US blockade of Iranian ports.

US officials have confirmed some of the details of the agreement, saying economic benefits for Iran would depend on Tehran meeting its obligations.

Previous reports from the US had suggested Lebanon may not be part of this deal - with Iran reportedly insisting on it.

In recent months, variations of an agreement have been expected several times but have not been completed in the later stages.

The war began with US and Israeli strikes across Iran on 28 February, prompting Iran to attack Israel and US-allied states in the Gulf - as well as effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route for the world's oil and liquefied natural gas.

title.en: Germany faces EU penalty over gender pay gap directive
title.zh: 德国因性别薪酬差距指令面临欧盟处罚

summary.en: Germany was required to incorporate the EU Pay Transparency Directive into its national law, but it has missed the deadline.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Germany was required to incorporate the EU Pay Transparency Directive into its national law, but it has missed the deadline.

Many people continue to earn less than others for the same job — often because of their gender. This is illegal, but difficult to prove. The EU Pay Transparency Directive, which takes effect across the European Union this month, is supposed to help make sure workers earn equal pay for the same job.

The new rules are designed to put more pressure on employers to ensure there is equal pay within their workforce. But Germany — the EU's largest, strongest, and most populous economy — has missed the June 7 deadline to implement the directive.

The pay gap between men and women in Germany remains an issue despite legal requirements to eliminate it. According to the German Federal Statistical Office, the adjusted gender pay gap was 6% in 2025, with women earning less than men in the same position and with the same qualifications.

The EU Pay Transparency Directive was introduced "to strengthen the application of equal pay for equal work or work of equal value between men and women through pay transparency and enforcement mechanisms." Once it takes effect, the idea is that employees should be able to request information to find out whether they are being paid unfairly for equivalent work and employers will be required to eliminated unjustified pay gaps.

The law relies on three mechanisms: The right to request information, gender pay gap reporting for larger companies, and joint pay assessments.

On May 6, the German government approved a bill to amend the General Equal Treatment Act (AGG) on the recommendation of German Education Minister Karin Prien, whose portfolio includes women's affairs, and Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig. The aim was to incorporate the EU's requirements into German law.  

"This is an important step toward putting our commitment to greater equality and effective action against discrimination into practice," said Prien. However, she attracted accusations that she had caved to the business lobby with her warning to "not place an unnecessary burden on government agencies and businesses and to keep procedures as simple as possible."

"The most important change is that anyone affected by discrimination will now have four months, rather than two, to decide whether they want to assert a claim according to the AGG," said Hubig as she presented the amendment. But this has apparently not convinced the European Commission.

title.en: Anthropic cuts top-tier AI access after US foreigner ban
title.zh: Anthropic因美国禁止外国人访问而切断顶级AI服务

summary.en: Anthropic, an AI firm, announced it was ordered to block foreign nationals from accessing its advanced Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models. This decision was made on national security grounds by the US government.
summary.zh: 人工智能公司Anthropic宣布，已接到命令，禁止外国公民访问其先进的Fable 5和Mythos 5人工智能模型。美国政府基于国家安全理由做出了这一决定。

body.en:
The firm said it was ordered to block foreign nationals from accessing its state of the art Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models on national security grounds.

Anthropic said Friday it has cut access to two powerful artificial intelligence (AI) models after a United States  government order citing national security concerns.

The sudden block marks a major escalation in Anthropic’s growing showdown with the Trump administration after failed negotiations earlier this year over potential US military and intelligence use of its technology .

The order is potentially a major setback for Anthropic's plans to take the company public  later this year.

The San Francisco-headquartered firm said in a statement that it received a directive to block its Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals.

Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are the newest versions of the Claude AI model, released on June 9. The first is widely available to the public, while the latter is mostly restricted to vetted organizations.

The company said the ban applied to foreigners "whether inside or outside the United States, including foreign national Anthropic employees."

However, Anthropic said it had blocked access for all customers for now to ensure compliance.

"Our understanding is that the [US] government believes it has become aware of a method of bypassing, or 'jailbreaking' Fable," the statement continued.

It said the company's own tests found only a small number of already-known bugs that were "minor vulnerabilities."

Anthropic said it was complying with the directive, but disagreed that the US government's findings "should be cause for recalling a commercial model deployed to hundreds of millions of people."

It added that if this rule were applied across AI platforms, "we believe it would essentially halt all new model deployments for all frontier model providers."

Anthropic’s relationship with the US government broke down this year after the company refused to allow the military to use its AI models for domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons systems.

In response, the Pentagon added Anthropic to a supply chain blacklist , which is set to take effect later this year and could severely limit the company’s federal contracts.

This latest export ban marks the second major action by the Trump administration against the AI firm in just a few months.

The New York Times described the order as "unusually expansive," noting it could prevent Anthropic's employees in allied nations, including Canada or the United Kingdom, from using the AI models.

body.zh: 该公司表示，以国家安全为由，其被勒令禁止外国人访问其最先进的《神鬼寓言 5》和《神话 5》人工智能模型。 Anthropic 周五表示，在美国政府以国家安全为由发布命令后，该公司已切断对两种强大人工智能 (AI) 模型的访问。 今年早些时候，就美国军事和情报部门可能使用其技术的谈判失败后，这次突然的封锁标志着 Anthropic 与特朗普政府日益激烈的对峙大幅升级。 该命令可能对 Anthropic 公司今年晚些时候上市的计划造成重大挫折。 这家总部位于旧金山的公司在一份声明中表示，它收到了一项指令，要求对所有外国人屏蔽其《克劳德寓言 5》和《克劳德神话 5》。 《神鬼寓言 5》和《神话 5》是 Claude AI 模型的最新版本，于 6 月 9 日发布。第一个版本广泛向公众开放，而后者主要仅限于经过审查的组织。 该公司表示，该禁令适用于“无论是美国境内还是境外的外国人，包括 Anthropic 的外籍员工”。 不过，Anthropic 表示，为了确保合规性，目前已禁止所有客户访问。 “我们的理解是，[美国]政府认为它已经意识到一种绕过或‘越狱’Fable 的方法，”声明继续说道。 该公司表示，该公司自己的测试只发现了少数已知的“小漏洞”漏洞。 Anthropic 表示，它正在遵守该指令，但不同意美国政府的调查结果“应该成为召回部署到数亿人的商业模式的理由”。 它补充说，如果这条规则适用于人工智能平台，“我们相信它基本上会停止所有前沿模型提供商的所有新模型部署。” Anthropic 与美国政府的关系今年破裂，因为该公司拒绝允许军方将其人工智能模型用于国内监视和完全自主武器系统。 作为回应，五角大楼将 Anthropic 添加到供应链黑名单中，该名单将于今年晚些时候生效，可能会严重限制该公司的联邦合同。 这项最新的出口禁令标志着特朗普政府在短短几个月内针对这家人工智能公司采取的第二次重大行动。 《纽约时报》将这一命令描述为“异常广泛”，并指出它可能会阻止 Anthropic 在包括加拿大或英国在内的盟国的员工使用人工智能模型。 本月早些时候，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普签署了一项行政命令，要求联邦政府对最先进的人工智能系统进行国家安全审查……

title.en: US, Venezuela say Tren de Aragua leader killed in strike
title.zh: 美国和委内瑞拉称“阿拉瓜列车”帮派头目在袭击中丧生

summary.en: US President Donald Trump announced that the leader of the Venezuela-based Tren de Aragua gang, which Washington has designated a terrorist organization, was killed in a US strike.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普宣布，委内瑞拉“阿拉瓜列车”帮派的头目在美国的一次袭击中丧生。华盛顿已将该帮派列为恐怖组织。

body.en:
The leader of the Venezuela-based Tren de Aragua gang has died in a US strike, US President Donald Trump says. The gang has been labeled a terrorist organization by Washington.

The leader of the notorious Tren de Agua gang, Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, has been killed in a US strike in Venezuela , US President Donald Trump said on Friday.

The Trump administration has repeatedly accused Tren de Aragua of being behind much of the violence and drug dealing in many US cities.

Venezuela has confirmed the death of Guerrero Flores, saying he was killed during a "joint operation" with the US in the southeastern state of Bolivar.

Trump said the US had carried out a "swift and lethal kinetic" strike to kill Guerrero Flores, whom he called "the infamous leader” of the Tren de Aragua gang.

In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump wrote that "Tren de Aragua terrorists no longer have safe haven in Venezuela or anywhere else and, under my leadership, we will find these vicious murderers and drug lords anytime, anyplace, and send them to the depths of hell where they belong."

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth posted on X that the strike was carried out earlier in the week on one of the gang's compounds in Venezuela.

Rewards of up to $5 million (€4.32 million) had been offered by the US State Department for information that led to Guerrero Flores' arrest.

Venezuela's Ministry of Communications has confirmed the death in a statement about the operation at the compound. 

"There were clashes with members of these criminal structures, in which Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, alias 'Nino Guerrero,' was neutralized," it said.

Tren de Aragua came into being more than 10 years ago at a prison in Venezuela's central state of Aragua, where Guerrero Flores and other inmates took over control and administration as the country's economic crisis led to a neglect of jails.

Their power over the prison was such that they were able to turn the facility into a city-like structure with its own zoo, baseball field, casino and restaurants. 

The gang then expanded transnationally as  millions of Venezuelans emigrated in search of a better life.

Several countries, including Peru and Colombia, have accused the group of being behind rising violence in the region.

Guerrero Flores himself had racketeering, drug and firearms charges filed against him New York in December.

The Trump administration has also heavily targeted the gang, among other things with strikes in the eastern Pacific Ocean and Caribbean on small boats it says are smuggling drugs to the US.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，总部位于委内瑞拉的特伦·德·阿拉瓜帮派头目在美国的袭击中身亡。该团伙已被华盛顿列为恐怖组织。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周五表示，臭名昭著的特伦·德·阿瓜帮派的头目赫克托·鲁斯滕福德·格雷罗·弗洛雷斯在美国对委内瑞拉的一次袭击中被杀。 特朗普政府多次指责特伦·德阿拉瓜是美国许多城市暴力和毒品交易的幕后黑手。 委内瑞拉证实了格雷罗·弗洛雷斯的死亡，称他是在与美国在东南部玻利瓦尔州的一次“联合行动”中被杀的。 特朗普表示，美国发动了“迅速而致命的动能”打击，杀死了格雷罗·弗洛雷斯，他称他为特伦·德·阿拉瓜帮的“臭名昭著的头目”。 特朗普在其“真相社交”平台上发帖写道，“特伦德阿拉瓜恐怖分子在委内瑞拉或其他任何地方都不再有避难所，在我的领导下，我们将随时随地找到这些恶毒的杀人犯和毒枭，并将他们送入他们所属的地狱深处。” 国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯 (Pete Hegseth) 在 X 上发帖称，本周早些时候，该团伙在委内瑞拉的一处营地遭到了袭击。 美国国务院悬赏高达 500 万美元（432 万欧元），奖励提供导致格雷罗·弗洛雷斯被捕的信息。 委内瑞拉交通部在一份有关该院落行动的声明中证实了这起死亡事件。 声明称：“与这些犯罪组织的成员发生了冲突，赫克托·鲁斯滕福德·格雷罗·弗洛雷斯（Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores，别名‘尼诺·格雷罗’）在冲突中被消灭。” 十多年前，特伦·德·阿拉瓜诞生于委内瑞拉中部阿拉瓜州的一所监狱，由于该国的经济危机导致监狱被忽视，格雷罗·弗洛雷斯和其他囚犯接管了监狱的控制和管理。 他们对监狱的权力如此之大，以至于他们能够将监狱变成一座类似城市的建筑，拥有自己的动物园、棒球场、赌场和餐馆。 随着数百万委内瑞拉人为了寻求更好的生活而移民，该团伙随后向跨国扩张。 包括秘鲁和哥伦比亚在内的多个国家指责该组织是该地区暴力事件不断升级的幕后黑手。 去年 12 月，格雷罗·弗洛雷斯 (Guerrero Flores) 本人在纽约遭到敲诈勒索、毒品和枪支指控。 特朗普政府还重点打击了该团伙，其中包括在东太平洋和加勒比海地区袭击了据称向美国走私毒品的小船。 特朗普过去曾声称该团伙在委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗的控制下运作，...

reflection.en: The news of a violent gang leader's death in a strike brings to mind the somber truth that those who live by violence often meet a violent end. This outcome, while perhaps bringing a sense of justice, reminds us of the destructive cycle that violence perpetuates in the world.

title.en: Mercenaries and high-profile defectors abound in Sudan war
title.zh: 苏丹战争中雇佣兵和引人注目的叛逃者比比皆是

summary.en: Human rights organizations accuse the UAE of supporting the RSF militia, which has seen a number of high-profile defections to the Sudanese Armed Forces. Meanwhile, the civilian population continues to suffer.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Human rights organizations accuse the UAE of supporting the RSF militia, which has seen a number of high-profile defections to the Sudanese Armed Forces. Meanwhile, the civilian population continues to suffer.

When Sudan's military leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan welcomed Al-Nour Ahmed Adam — also known as Al-Nour Al-Qubba and a former senior commander of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia — into the ranks of the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) earlier this year, it was one of the most high-profile defections in the Sudanese civil war to date.

While the SAF controls the capital Khartoum, Port Sudan and large parts of the east and center of the country, its rival RSF holds vast areas in the west of the country, particularly in Darfur, including the city of El Fasher.

Al-Nour Al-Qubba is not the only defector: He was followed a few weeks later by high-ranking RSF commander, Ali Rizq Allah, also known as Al-Savannah.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) has reviewed videos purportedly showing these two defectors during the siege of El Fasher, where the international NGO has documented war crimes committed by the RSF , led by General Mohamed Hamdan Daglo, commonly known as Hemedti, during the city's capture in October 2025.

Since the war began in 2023 , Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has been trying to recruit defectors from the RSF into the SAF. Almost from the beginning, he declared a general amnesty for members of the militia if they laid down their arms, saying they could be integrated into the military. Human Rights Watch says it was unable to verify whether this also applied to the most recent defectors.

For Mohamed Osman, a Sudan researcher at Human Rights Watch, there must not be impunity. "Those responsible for serious international crimes and human rights violations do not get a free pass if they switch sides," he said, adding that "Sudanese people who have experienced horrific abuses under any commander's watch deserve justice."

According to conflict monitors at Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED), the recent defections could be a sign of increasing tension within the RSF ranks and of "cracks in the RSF's core alliances." They assume that "local loyalties are superseding central command, sparking violent intra-coalition competition over remaining war spoils."

The defections come at a time when both the SAF and the RSF have external support. Though the front is in Sudan, the alliances that are keeping the war going extend far beyond the country's borders. The RSF's supporters are believed to include the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Ethiopia , Libya , Chad and Kenya . body.zh: 人权组织指责阿联酋支持 RSF 民兵，该民兵中有许多引人注目的叛逃者加入苏丹武装部队。与此同时，平民继续遭受苦难。 今年早些时候，苏丹军事领导人阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·布尔汉 (Abdel Fattah al-Burhan) 欢迎努尔·艾哈迈德·亚当 (Al-Nour Ahmed Adam)（又名 Al-Nour Al-Qubba，快速支援部队 (RSF) 民兵前高级指挥官）加入苏丹武装部队 (SAF) 队伍，这是迄今为止苏丹内战中最引人注目的叛逃事件之一。 虽然苏丹武装部队控制着首都喀土穆、苏丹港以及该国东部和中部的大部分地区，但其竞争对手无国界武装部队控制着该国西部的大片地区，特别是在达尔富尔，包括法希尔市。 努尔·库巴并不是唯一的叛逃者：几周后，无国界部队高级指挥官阿里·里兹克·阿拉（Ali Rizq Allah，也被称为阿尔·萨凡纳）也追随了他。 人权观察组织 (HRW) 审查了据称显示这两名叛逃者在法希尔围困期间的视频，该国际非政府组织记录了穆罕默德·哈姆丹·达格洛将军（俗称赫梅蒂）领导的无国界部队在 2025 年 10 月占领该市期间犯下的战争罪行。 自 2023 年战争爆发以来，阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·布尔汉一直试图招募无国界医生组织的叛逃者加入苏丹武装部队。几乎从一开始，他就宣布对放下武器的民兵成员实行大赦，并称他们可以编入军队。人权观察表示，无法核实这是否也适用于最近的叛逃者。 对于人权观察组织的苏丹研究员穆罕默德·奥斯曼来说，决不能有罪不罚。他说：“那些对严重国际罪行和侵犯人权行为负有责任的人，如果他们倒戈，就不会获得自由通行证。”他补充说，“在任何指挥官的监督下经历过可怕虐待的苏丹人民都应该受到正义的对待。” 根据武装冲突地点和事件数据项目 (ACLED) 的冲突监测员的说法，最近的叛逃可能是无国界医生组织内部紧张局势加剧以及“无国界医生组织核心联盟出现裂痕”的迹象。他们认为“地方忠诚正在取代中央指挥，引发了联盟内部对剩余战利品的激烈竞争。” 这些叛逃发生在新加坡武装部队和无国界部队都得到外部支持的情况下。尽管前线在苏丹，但维持战争持续的联盟却远远超出了该国的边界。据信，无国界医生组织的支持者包括阿拉伯联合酋长国（阿联酋）、埃塞俄比亚、利比亚、乍得和肯尼亚。苏丹武装部队也被指控犯有战争罪，得到埃及、沙特阿拉伯、土耳其和厄立特里亚的支持。伊朗还被怀疑提供了军事...

title.en: Why the Socceroos may have seen a dingo at their Californian World Cup training ground
title.zh: 本土联系和“矿物魔力”助力澳大利亚男足世界杯征程

summary.en: Australians are showing up in unlikely places to help with the Socceroos' preparation for the FIFA World Cup 2026.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚人正在意想不到的地方出现，帮助澳大利亚男足备战2026年国际足联世界杯。

body.en:
The Socceroos have been preparing at their California base for their first FIFA World Cup match, on a world-class pitch engineered by an Australian abroad.

The Australian side will take on Türkiye in Vancouver on Sunday afternoon Australian time.

They are now based at the Oakland Roots/Soul Training Facility, which is run by the football club of the same name.

The former home of the Oakland Raiders NFL team is also run by groundskeeper and facility manager Marc Logan, who speaks with a strong Australian accent.

Having lived in the US for 27 years, Logan said he was "ecstatic" when he learned that Australia's national football team would be based at the training ground he looks after.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Logan said he mixes a product called Mineral Magic — which comes from Western Australia — with the Californian soil under the immaculate pitches at the facility.

"It's an amorphous silica, and we've been using it for a number of years," Logan explained, adding that he hopes the product's Australian link will help power the Socceroos to strong World Cup performances.

Logan brought another reminder of home with him to California — a model of a dingo.

"I thought, 'what the heck?' I needed to have a dingo, just so I could say, has anybody seen my dingo?" he said.

"So it was important that I keep a little bit of Australia here. I've got a dingo here [to keep] the birds away."

The Roots are the club's men's team. They play in the US second professional tier. The Soul are the women's team, and play at amateur level.

In Alameda, where the club is based, the local community is known for its rich diversity.

Edreece Arghandiwal, co-founder of the Oakland Roots/Soul Club, told SBS News that football has had a "resounding effect" on his life.

He recalled that, when he arrived as a refugee aged five — along with his family and other members of the Afghan community — football "created a sense of identity and purpose in this community".

Arghandiwal said the small connections between the club and Australia through people like Logan were "once in a lifetime" stories.

"I think that all of this has aligned for some reason beyond us and I'm hopeful that that reason is Australia going very far in the tournament," he said.

"It's a benefit to us, it's a benefit to the entire nation, and we're really wishing them all here."

In another surprising twist, the club's left-back Jesus de Vincente used to live not far from Mat Ryan, Australia's veteran goalkeeper, and his mum works at Ryan's Spanish club, Levante.

title.en: Australia is facing an El Niño. Experts say it won't be a 'super' event
title.zh: 澳大利亚面临厄尔尼诺现象，专家称其不会是“超级”事件

summary.en: Australia is preparing for an El Niño weather pattern, though experts predict it will not be a severe "super" event, contrasting with the triple La Niña experienced from 2020 to 2022.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚正准备迎接厄尔尼诺天气模式，但专家预测它不会是严重的“超级”事件，这与2020年至2022年经历的三重拉尼娜现象形成对比。

body.en:
As the weather changes, concerns are rising for a possible extreme El Niño.

However, weather experts aren't convinced that this year's El Niño event will be anything out of the ordinary.

El Niño and La Niña are part of a naturally occurring weather cycle, the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO).

The ENSO typically operates over one to eight years and alternates between periods of warming (El Niño) and cooling (La Niña) in the eastern and central tropical Pacific.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The tropical Pacific is the warm, equatorial region of the Pacific Ocean, which stretches along almost one-third of the Earth's surface, along the equator.

It's an area responsible for much global climate regulation and weather patterns.

Rising sea surface temperature in this region and weakened equatorial trade winds cause an El Niño.

For Australia, El Niño brings reduced rainfall, warmer temperatures, a shift in temperature extremes, increased frost risk, decreased alpine snow depths and increased fire danger in southeast regions.

Winds change ocean surface currents and pull cold water from the sea depths to the surface, lowering the sea surface temperature.

La Niña in Australia can mean increased rainfall, cooler daytime temperatures and warmer overnight temperatures, a shift in temperature extremes, decreased frost risk, increased tropical cyclone events and earlier monsoon onset.

On 2 June, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) announced the formation of an El Niño.

Less than a week later, the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration predicted that there's a 63 per cent chance the El Niño event would become "very strong".

While some scientists define an El Niño as a temperature anomaly of 0.5 degrees Celsius above average, Australia's Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) defines an El Niño as 0.8 degrees Celsius above average.

For a super or extreme El Niño, sea surface temperature would be at least 2 to 2.5 degrees Celsius warmer than average.

A super El Niño can disrupt atmospheric circulation, leading to severe weather events such as thunderstorms and tropical cyclones in the eastern equatorial region.

For the western Pacific region, which includes Australia, super El Niños can cause devastating droughts and wildfires — including the Ash Wednesday bushfires of February 1983.

Super El Niños can cause an increased decline in marine life, and massive global economic loss.

The chances of a super El Niño in 2026 are slim, particularly because it follows a triple La Niña between late 2020 and mid-2022.

title.en: Jessie J’s triumphant return puts lucrative Chinese market in spotlight
title.zh: Jessie J的凯旋归来使利润丰厚的中国市场备受关注

summary.en: British pop star Jessie J made a triumphant return to the lucrative Chinese music market, a week after announcing she was cancer-free. Her success in the country's music scene has inspired other Western acts to seek similar opportunities since her breakout in 2018.
summary.zh: 英国流行歌星Jessie J在宣布自己“癌症痊愈”一周后，凯旋回归利润丰厚的中国音乐市场。自2018年她在中国取得突破性成功以来，她的经历也激励了其他西方艺人寻求类似的机会。

body.en: Other western acts have attempted to crack country’s music scene since singer’s breakout success in 2018 One week after announcing she was “cancer free”, the British pop star Jessie J did what any recovering patient would do and travelled thousands of miles around the world to perform for an audience of more than a billion people. On 29 May, the singer-songwriter, whose real name is Jessica Cornish, belted out a stage-rattling rendition of Frank Sinatra’s My Way on the stage of Singer, a hugely popular Chinese singing competition similar to The Voice. She also performed her new song, California, briefly adapting the lyrics to change California to Changsha, the Chinese city where Singer is hosted. Continue reading...

reflection.en: After facing a serious illness, Jessie J's return to the stage embodies a powerful message of renewed strength and purpose. Her journey reminds us that even after periods of great weakness, there is hope for soaring again, finding fresh vigor for the path ahead.
reflection.zh: 面对重疾之后，Jessie J重返舞台，这体现了力量和目标重获新生的有力信息。她的旅程提醒我们，即使在极度虚弱之后，仍有希望再次翱翔，为前方的道路找到新的活力。

summary.en: A US academic, Min Zin, known for his writings on Myanmar and Chinese foreign policy, has been arrested in China on suspicion of engaging in espionage activities. This arrest occurred just a month after a high-profile visit by the US President to Beijing.

body.en: Arrest of Min Zin, who writes about Myanmar and Chinese foreign policy, comes just month after Trump visit to Beijing China has arrested a US scholar who writes about Myanmar and Chinese foreign policy on suspicion of spying. Min Zin was suspected of “engaging in espionage activities that endanger China’s national security,” China’s ministry of foreign affairs spokesperson, Lin Jian, said on Friday. Continue reading...

summary.en: China's Ministry of State Security has alleged that foreign intelligence agencies are employing "spy turtles" and "spy fish" equipped with sensors to gather sensitive data in Chinese waters. The ministry described these activities as part of an "invisible secret war."

title.en: China has long sought to control women’s bodies. Increasingly, they’re making their own choices
title.zh: 中国长期寻求控制女性身体，但她们正日益做出自己的选择

summary.en: Chinese women are increasingly asserting their reproductive choices, pushing back against decades of state control, including the lasting impact of the one-child policy. Since 1949, the state has historically dictated women's bodies and labor.
summary.zh: 面对国家长期以来的压力以及独生子女政策的深远影响，越来越多的中国女性正在自主做出她们的生育选择。自1949年中华人民共和国成立以来，女性的身体一直被视为国家事务。

body.en: More women are rejecting state pressure over their reproductive choices, amid the devastating legacy of the one-child policy Ever since the founding of the People’s Republic of China in 1949, women’s bodies have been the business of the state. In the 1950s, labour for state-controlled work units was organised according to women’s menstrual cycles. Then for decades, there was the one-child policy. Across vast swathes of the country the policy was enforced with a brutal severity. As well as fines for additional children, women were forced to have abortions and subjected to forced sterilisations. Continue reading...

summary.en: A Thai court has sentenced two Uyghur men to death for their involvement in the 2015 Bangkok bombing at the Erawan Shrine, which killed 20 people and injured 120.

The explosion occurred at the Erawan Shrine in the centre of Bangkok, an area popular with foreign tourists. As well as the 20 people killed, another 120 were injured. title.zh: 中国比亚迪目标五年内成为全球最大汽车公司

title.zh: 在中国，女性的处境日益艰难，但在成都，女性专属空间却蓬勃发展

summary.en: In Chengdu, China, a cautious feminist revival is taking root through female-only spaces, despite official concerns about women rejecting traditional roles. These communities offer women a discreet environment to envision a more equal future.

body.en: The socially relaxed city has seen a cautious feminist revival despite authorities’ growing alarm at women who shun traditional roles In a small, unassuming bookstore in south-west China, a discreet community of women dream of a more equal future. Here in Chengdu, 42-year-old Shen Shen runs one of the country’s leading feminist bookstores. “The world doesn’t lack bookstores for men,” she says, surrounded by piles of volumes by authors including Judith Butler, Simone de Beauvoir and Chizuko Ueno . Continue reading...

title.en: 'Important consensus': What we know about Xi Jinping's North Korean visit
title.zh: “重要共识”：我们对习近平访问朝鲜的了解

summary.en: The Chinese President has made his first visit to North Korea since 2019, marking an important diplomatic engagement between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国国家主席自2019年以来首次访问朝鲜，标志着两国之间一次重要的外交接触。

body.en:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has visited North Korea for a series of meetings with leader Kim Jong Un.

The pair reached an "important consensus" on the nation's ties in a "new era", according to Xi.

Xi arrived in the North Korean capital Pyongyang on Monday for his first official visit to the diplomatically isolated nation since 2019.

He travelled with his wife and several other top officials for a two-day trip, he said, aimed to bring ties between the longtime partners to "new heights".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The visit follows Xi's hosting of a string of world leaders, including US President Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin, in Beijing.

State media images showed Xi and Kim beaming as they shook hands, with the Chinese leader receiving a lavish welcome ceremony featuring a red-carpet military salute and cheering crowds.

Xi said he had reached "an important consensus with Kim on developing China-DPRK relations in the new era", China's Xinhua news agency reported, using North Korea's official acronym.

The leaders agreed to put the two nations' friendly relations "on a more solid basis", North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency said.

Chinese state media reported Xi told Kim their countries "should strengthen exchanges in diplomacy, law enforcement [and] the military" and expand economic cooperation.

He also called for expanded economic cooperation, citing the recent reopening of border crossings and transport links.

China has long been North Korea's largest economic partner, with US and South Korean estimates indicating that China has accounted for almost all of North Korea's annual foreign trade in recent years.

In March, flights and passenger train services between the two nations resumed after a six-year hiatus due to pandemic-era border closures and their aftermath.

Official readouts and state media reports have not said whether Xi and Kim discussed North Korea's nuclear weapons development, for which the nation languishes under international sanctions.

Last month, the White House announced that the Chinese leader and Trump had "confirmed their shared goal to denuclearise North Korea" during their summit in Beijing.

Kim has repeatedly vowed never to give up his nuclear arsenal, and his sister said before Xi's visit that the program was North Korea's "line of no retreat".

The absence of denuclearisation from official statements means the summit effectively "appeared to have been a forum where China granted Pyongyang's rights to nuclear weapons", Lee Ho-ryung of the Korea Institute for Defence Analyses told AFP.

In return, it appears Kim supported China's "One-China principle regarding Taiwan", she added,...
body.zh: 中国国家主席习近平访问朝鲜并与领导人金正恩进行了一系列会晤。 习近平表示，两国元首就“新时代”两国关系达成“重要共识”。 习近平周一抵达朝鲜首都平壤，这是他自 2019 年以来首次对这个外交孤立国家进行正式访问。 他说，他与妻子和其他几位高级官员一起进行了为期两天的旅行，旨在将这两个长期合作伙伴之间的关系提升到“新的高度”。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 此次访问之前，习近平在北京接待了包括美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京在内的一系列世界领导人。 官方媒体画面显示，习近平和金正恩握手时笑容满面，中国领导人接受了盛大的欢迎仪式，包括红地毯军礼和欢呼的人群。 据中国新华社报道，习近平表示，他“同金正恩就发展新时代中朝关系达成重要共识”。 朝鲜官方通讯社朝中社称，两国领导人同意将两国友好关系建立在“更坚实的基础上”。 中国官方媒体报道称，习近平告诉金正恩，两国“应加强外交、执法[和]军事方面的交流”并扩大经济合作。 他还呼吁扩大经济合作，并列举了最近重新开放的过境点和运输线路。 中国长期以来一直是朝鲜最大的经济伙伴，美国和韩国的估计表明，中国近年来几乎占据了朝鲜年度对外贸易的全部。 今年三月，两国之间的航班和客运列车服务在因大流行时期边境关闭及其后果而中断六年后恢复。 官方消息和官方媒体报道均未提及习近平和金正恩是否讨论了朝鲜的核武器开发问题，该国因核武器开发而受到国际制裁。 上个月，白宫宣布中国领导人和特朗普在北京峰会期间“确认了朝鲜无核化的共同目标”。 金正恩一再发誓永远不会放弃他的核武库，他的妹妹在习近平访问之前表示，该计划是朝鲜的“不退路”。 韩国国防分析研究所的李浩良告诉法新社，官方声明中没有无核化，这意味着这次峰会实际上“似乎是中国授予平壤核武器权利的论坛”。 她补充说，作为回报，金正恩似乎支持中国的“一个中国原则”。

reflection.en: High-level diplomatic visits like this one underscore the complex decisions leaders face in international relations. Proverbs reminds us that nations find stability and safety when guided by wise counsel. reflection.zh: 像这样的高层外交访问，突显了领导人在国际关系中面临的复杂决策。箴言提醒我们，国家在有明智的指导时才能找到稳定和安全。在一个联盟错综复杂、挑战重重的世界里，寻求广博的智慧对于驾驭地缘政治格局至关重要。

title.en: As voter disillusionment grows, why aren't voters flocking to the Greens in Australia?
title.zh: 随着选民的幻想破灭，为什么选民没有涌向澳大利亚的绿党呢？

summary.en: Growing voter dissatisfaction with mainstream politics has led to a rise in popularity for One Nation. The same cannot be said for the Greens.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The rise of One Nation may not come as a surprise to anyone who has been watching politics in the US, the UK and the rest of Europe in recent years.

But Australia's belated embrace of right-wing populism is perhaps more unusual because of what has happened on the other side of the political spectrum.

Why have the Greens not been able to capitalise on disillusion with mainstream parties and the hollowing out of the political centre, as their counterparts in the US and the UK have?

Since the last federal election in May 2025, One Nation has surged in opinion polls to become the most popular party in the land, with about 30 per cent of the first-preference vote.

The Greens, meanwhile, have barely budged from their haul of 12 per cent at the last election.

In the same period, the Green Party of England and Wales, under leader Zack Polanski, has increased its voter share from 10 per cent to 18 per cent in recent local government elections.

It turns out they are but only in certain demographics, Redbridge polling analyst Kos Samaras says.

Among Generation Z voters, who were born after 1996, the Greens vote is more than 30 per cent — significantly higher than that of millennial voters at the same age.

"Generation Z is absolutely different to every other generation that's come before them," Samaras told the Australian Associated Press (AAP).

The reason the overall Greens vote has stayed relatively stable is that they're losing support amongst older Australians — to Labor, the teal independents and, to a lesser extent, One Nation.

Polanski told a Victorian Greens conference in May the party needed to take on One Nation and connect with the anger of voters deserting the major parties.

Echoing Polanski, Greens leader Larissa Waters says her party is ready to replace Labor.

"What's clear is that people are now realising that the system is stacked against them, and that the major parties don't actually want to change that system, and so they're looking for an alternative," she says.

"What they will soon come to realise is that One Nation is working for the same interests that are funding the Labor and Liberal parties."

Echoing New York mayor Zohran Mamdani in the US, Waters says Australia needs to tax the one per cent, especially gas exporters.

In housing, she criticises the government for not going far enough on proposed tax reforms, arguing that grandfathering existing negative gearing and capital gains pulls the ladder up for future generations.

summary.en: For refugees who reach Australia, safety is one thing. Permanency is another — and it's becoming harder to win.

body.en:

Zuhria Al Hattab survived the night the sky fell on her grandmother's house in northern Gaza.

She survived the journey south — hands raised, white flag up — along a corridor the Israeli military had designated a 'safe route', until the bombs started raining again.

"The whole road was blood and martyrs and body parts, severed heads, severed hands," she tells SBS News of the aftermath of Israel's bombardment during the daytime truce.

"I was crying the whole way … but we had to keep walking continuously without stopping, not looking right or left."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Al Hattab and her wounded brother, Mohammed, survived the journey out — a $10,000 passage through Rafah into Egypt, brokered by her sister, already safe in Australia.

They reached Perth in 2024. But most of the relatives her sister had applied to bring to Australia — including their father and younger brothers — never made it out.

More than two years later, the 34-year-old primary school teacher is still struggling to rebuild her life. She now finds herself caught in a political reckoning over whether people like her should be allowed to stay.

For many Palestinians who escaped Gaza and made it to Australia, the journey to safety did not mark the end of upheaval. It was the beginning of a different kind of uncertainty.

Al Hattab holds a Temporary Humanitarian Concern visa, subclass 786, offered to Palestinians who fled to Australia after the conflict in Gaza escalated in October 2023.

The three-year visa — issued only on a case-by-case basis following mandatory health, character, and security checks — is the second step of the Australian government's Temporary Humanitarian Stay program.

It allows her to work, study and access Medicare, but expires in early 2028. Unlike the version offered to Ukrainians in the aftermath of Russia's invasion , it provides no pathway to permanent residency.

She is one of around 1,700 Palestinians who have arrived from Gaza, mostly on initial 12-month visitor visas — a cohort prioritised based on prior travel to Australia or strong family connections.

The federal government has issued about 3,000 visitor visas in total to Palestinians since October 2023.

However, like Al Hattab's relatives, hundreds of visa holders have been unable to leave Gaza, with Israel's siege and the closure of the strip's land crossings preventing their departure.

As the weather changes, concerns are rising for a possible extreme El Niño.

However, weather experts aren't convinced that this year's El Niño event will be anything out of the ordinary.

El Niño and La Niña are part of a naturally occurring weather cycle, the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO).

The ENSO typically operates over one to eight years and alternates between periods of warming (El Niño) and cooling (La Niña) in the eastern and central tropical Pacific.

The tropical Pacific is the warm, equatorial region of the Pacific Ocean, which stretches along almost one-third of the Earth's surface, along the equator.

It's an area responsible for much global climate regulation and weather patterns.

Rising sea surface temperature in this region and weakened equatorial trade winds cause an El Niño.

For Australia, El Niño brings reduced rainfall, warmer temperatures, a shift in temperature extremes, increased frost risk, decreased alpine snow depths and increased fire danger in southeast regions.

Winds change ocean surface currents and pull cold water from the sea depths to the surface, lowering the sea surface temperature.

La Niña in Australia can mean increased rainfall, cooler daytime temperatures and warmer overnight temperatures, a shift in temperature extremes, decreased frost risk, increased tropical cyclone events and earlier monsoon onset.

On 2 June, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) announced the formation of an El Niño.

Less than a week later, the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration predicted that there's a 63 per cent chance the El Niño event would become "very strong".

While some scientists define an El Niño as a temperature anomaly of 0.5 degrees Celsius above average, Australia's Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) defines an El Niño as 0.8 degrees Celsius above average.

For a super or extreme El Niño, sea surface temperature would be at least 2 to 2.5 degrees Celsius warmer than average.

A super El Niño can disrupt atmospheric circulation, leading to severe weather events such as thunderstorms and tropical cyclones in the eastern equatorial region.

For the western Pacific region, which includes Australia, super El Niños can cause devastating droughts and wildfires — including the Ash Wednesday bushfires of February 1983.

Super El Niños can cause an increased decline in marine life, and massive global economic loss.

The chances of a super El Niño in 2026 are slim, particularly because it follows a triple La Niña between late 2020 and mid-2022.

title.en: Woman fighting for her life after shark attack at popular Sydney beach
title.zh: 悉尼热门海滩发生鲨鱼袭击事件，女子生命垂危

summary.en: A woman is in critical condition, fighting for her life, after being attacked by a shark at a popular Sydney beach. She was airlifted to a hospital for urgent treatment for severe injuries to her limbs.
summary.zh: 一名女子在悉尼一个热门海滩遭到鲨鱼袭击后，生命垂危，正在与死神搏斗。她被空运到医院，接受了肢体严重受伤的紧急治疗。

body.en:
A woman is fighting for life after being mauled by a shark at one of Australia's busiest beaches.

The incident follows a recent spate of fatal attacks nationwide and has prompted calls for stronger shark mitigation strategies across NSW.

Emergency services were called to Coogee Beach in Sydney's eastern suburbs shortly after 11am on Saturday following reports a swimmer had been bitten by a shark.

Bystanders pulled her from the water and commenced first aid before emergency services arrived.

Police rendered first aid to the woman, believed to be aged in her 30s, who had suffered serious arm and leg injuries.

Ambulance paramedics then continued her treatment before police cleared nearby Coogee Oval to facilitate the landing of a CareFlight rescue helicopter.

The woman was taken to hospital "semi-conscious and breathing," Surf Life Saving NSW said in a statement.

"We are sending our best wishes to the woman involved and her family at this time, after another terrible shark incident on our coastline," chief executive Steve Pearce said.

Nearby beaches from Bondi to Maroubra would remain closed for at least 24 hours, Surf Life Saving NSW said.

The incident underscored the need for stronger protections for beachgoers across the state, Central Coast local councillor Jared Wright said.

"Coogee Beach does not have an active SLSNSW drone patrol or shark listening station," he said in a statement.

"I have always been of the view that these protection measures need to be rolled out at as many beaches as possible, as quickly as possible."

Drones were being used at 14 locations statewide on Saturday but not at Coogee, SLNSW said.

Additional drone surveillance has been organised for Bondi and Bronte beaches for Saturday and Sunday, with further flights in the area to be assessed.

The most recent fatal attack in Australian waters happened on June 6, when 35‑year‑old diver Daniel Turpin was bitten by a suspected 4.5‑metre shark while spearfishing with his family off Michaelmas Island near Albany.

His death followed the killing of 38‑year‑old Perth father Steven Mattaboni off Rottnest Island on 16 May, and 39‑year‑old Queensland spearfisher Michael Jensz at Kennedy Shoal south of Cairns on May 24.

Both Western Australian attacks are believed to have involved great whites, while evidence points to Jensz having been taken by a bull shark.

In January, NSW made international headlines after recording four shark attacks in 48 hours.

Two resulted in people being hospitalised in critical condition, while the other two escaped without serious injuries.

In moments of severe injury and trauma, we hold onto the hope that God is near to those who are hurting. He is able to heal the brokenhearted and bind up their wounds, offering comfort and strength in the midst of suffering.

title.en: 'Give us a chance': Why experience isn't enough for many migrants in Australia
title.zh: “给我们一个机会”：为什么在澳大利亚，经验对许多移民来说还不够

summary.en: Australia has welcomed one million refugees since World War Two, yet many face unemployment or underemployment despite their qualifications and experience.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚自二战以来已安置了一百万名难民，但其中许多人尽管拥有技能，却仍面临失业或就业不足的困境。

body.en:
When Natalia Akulova arrived in Australia as a refugee in 2022, she brought university degrees, years of professional experience, and hopes of rebuilding her career.

Days after arriving, the 36-year-old mother of two visited the Sydney Opera House, fulfilling a dream she had held while living in Ukraine.

This month, Akulova graduated from a pilot employment project run by the opera house, designed to help skilled refugees enter the workforce.

"The eight-week cadetship helped me build confidence in job interview skills and communicate with people," she tells SBS News.

This week, Australia celebrates the one million refugees who have settled here since the end of World War Two.

The federal government's Humanitarian Program is set to remain at 20,000 places in 2026-27.

However, migration has become an increasingly contested political issue, with debates over housing affordability, infrastructure and population growth dominating public discourse.

The Opposition, led by Angus Taylor, has proposed capping net overseas migration at the number of new homes completed each year, arguing migration levels should be aligned with housing supply.

A recent opinion poll showed Pauline Hanson's One Nation party drawing ahead of the ruling Labor Party for the first time, with multiple surveys placing the populist party in the lead.

Professor Betina Szkudlarek and her research team at the University of Sydney Business School investigate the systemic challenges that skilled refugees face when seeking employment.

She says the shift in political sentiment could negatively affect those on humanitarian visas.

"I am concerned that, unfortunately, the current increasing anti-migration rhetoric will have a negative impact on refugees and refugee employment more broadly," Szkudlarek tells SBS News.

Szkudlarek says the debate's impact is also being felt in the labour market, where misconceptions about refugee workers persist among some employers.

She also points to growing challenges as some diversity and inclusion initiatives are being scaled back in parts of the corporate sector.

For many refugees, arriving in Australia marks not only a geographical shift but also a professional one.

Despite holding degrees and years of experience, many struggle to have their qualifications recognised, and often find themselves in jobs below their skill level and out of work altogether.

Akulova says she had strong professional experience in information technology before arriving, but entering the Australian job market was far from straightforward.
